source_note: General meaning of the words, written by the teacher. These are not Bible text. Bible references show where the word appears in the story.

def: Parents means a mother and a father.
A child has parents. Some parents are young. Some parents are old.
Another way to say it: a mother and a father.
entries.example: His parents are alive.
entries.contrast: A parent is one person. Parents are two or more.

qa.q: Is a parent one person or two people?

def: A Pharisee is a religious teacher in the Bible time.
The Pharisees know the law. They teach the people.
They are serious about the rules of God.
entries.example: The Pharisees ask many questions.
entries.contrast: A Pharisee is not a doctor. A Pharisee is not a king.

qa.q: Does a Pharisee teach the law?

def: A disciple is a person who follows a teacher and learns from him.
A disciple listens. A disciple asks questions.
Another way to say it: a student who follows.
entries.example: The disciples ask Jesus a question.
entries.contrast: A disciple is not a boss. A disciple learns.

qa.q: Does a disciple teach or learn?

def: A witness is a person who saw something. He tells others what he saw.
In a court, a witness says, "I saw this."
A witness does not guess. He tells what he knows.
entries.example: The man is a witness. He says, "This happened to me."
entries.contrast: A witness is not a person who guesses.

qa.q: Does a witness guess?

def: Blind means you cannot see. The eyes do not work.
A blind person cannot see the sun or a face.
Blind is not the same as dark. Dark means there is no light.
From birth means from the first day of life.
entries.example: The man was blind from birth.
entries.contrast: Blind is not deaf. A deaf person cannot hear.

qa.q: Can a blind man see?

def: Brave means you are not afraid, and you do the right thing.
A brave person speaks, even when it is hard.
Another way to say it: not afraid.
entries.example: The man is brave. He tells the leaders the truth.
entries.contrast: The opposite is afraid.

qa.q: Is a brave man afraid?

def: Honest means you say the truth. You do not lie.
An honest friend says, "I broke the cup." He does not say, "I did not."
Another way to say it: he tells the truth.
entries.example: He is honest. In other words, he doesn't lie.
entries.contrast: Lie means you say something that is not true.

qa.q: Does an honest man lie?

def: Direct means you say what you think. You say it clearly. You do not hide it.
A direct man does not hide the truth. He says it.
Another way to say it: he says it clearly.
entries.example: He is a direct man.
entries.contrast: The opposite is: he hides what he thinks.

qa.q: Does a direct man hide the truth?

def: Clever means you think fast and well.
A clever child learns fast. A clever answer is a good answer.
Another way to say it: smart.
entries.example: He is clever. He gives a good answer.
entries.contrast: Clever is not the same as strong.

qa.q: Is a clever person a person who thinks well?

def: Logical means the reasons fit together.
A logical answer has a clear reason: A, so B.
Another way to say it: it makes sense.
entries.example: His answer is logical.
entries.contrast: Not logical means: it does not make sense.

qa.q: Does a logical answer make sense?

def: Proud means you feel very good about yourself. You think you are better than other people.
A proud man says, "I am the best." He does not listen.
But a mother can be proud of her son. That is a good feeling. She is happy about him.
entries.example: The Pharisees are proud. They do not listen to the man.
entries.contrast: Proud is not humble. A humble man does not say, "I am better."

qa.q: Does a proud man listen?

def: Patient means you can wait. You do not get angry fast.
A patient teacher says the same thing again and again. He does not shout.
A patient man waits in a long line and stays calm.
entries.example: A patient teacher explains again.
entries.contrast: The opposite is impatient. An impatient man says, "Hurry up."

qa.q: Does a patient man get angry fast?

def: Grateful means you feel thank you inside.
Someone did something good for you, and you remember it.
A grateful man says thank you, and he means it.
entries.example: The man is grateful. Now he can see.
entries.contrast: Grateful is not angry. Grateful is warm.

qa.q: Does a grateful man say thank you?

def: Kind means you help people. You are good to others.
A kind teacher is good to the children.
Another way to say it: good to people.
entries.example: Jesus is kind. He helps the man.
entries.contrast: The opposite is unkind. An unkind man is bad to others.

qa.q: Does a kind man help people?

def: Powerful means you can do very big things.
A powerful machine can lift a car.
Only a powerful person can do this miracle.
entries.example: Jesus healed a man who was blind from birth.
entries.contrast: Powerful is not weak. A weak man cannot lift much.

qa.q: Can a powerful person do big things?

def: Serious means you think about important things, and you do not joke.
A serious teacher does not laugh in class.
A serious problem is a big problem.
entries.example: The Pharisees are serious about the law.
entries.contrast: Serious is not funny. A funny man makes you laugh.

qa.q: Does a serious teacher joke in class?

def: Afraid means you feel fear. You think something bad can happen.
A child is afraid of the dark. A person can be afraid of a big dog.
We say: afraid of something.
entries.example: The parents are afraid of the leaders.
entries.contrast: The opposite is not afraid. A brave man is not afraid.

qa.q: Are the parents afraid, or not afraid?

def: Angry means you feel hot inside because something is wrong.
An angry person talks loud. An angry person can say bad words.
We say: angry with a person, angry about a thing.
entries.example: The leaders are angry with the man.
entries.contrast: The opposite is calm. A calm man is not angry.

qa.q: Is a calm man angry?

def: Heal means to make a sick person well.
A doctor can heal a broken arm. After it is healed, the arm works again.
Heal is not the same as help. You help a sick man with water. You heal him when he is well.
entries.example: Jesus healed the blind man. Before, he could not see. After, he could see.
entries.contrast: Heal is not break. Break means to make something not work.

qa.q: Did Jesus heal the man?

def: A miracle is something that only God can do. People cannot do it.
A man who is blind from birth cannot see. When he suddenly sees, that is a miracle.
A miracle is not normal. It does not happen every day.
entries.example: The Bible tells about many miracles.
entries.contrast: A miracle is not a trick. A trick is something a man does to look strange.

qa.q: Can a person do a miracle alone?

def: Doubt means you are not sure. You think, "Maybe it is true, maybe not."
When you doubt, you do not say no. You say, "I am not sure."
The opposite is believe.
entries.example: Some people doubt the man.
entries.contrast: Doubt is not the same as no.

qa.q: Does a person who doubts say yes?

def: Believe means you think something is true. You trust it.
A child believes his mother. He trusts her words.
Believe is a very important word in the Bible.
entries.example: The man believes in Jesus.
entries.contrast: The opposite is doubt.

qa.q: Does a child believe his mother?

def: See means you use your eyes. You know what is in front of you.
You see the sun. You see a face. You see a book.
See is the opposite of blind.
entries.example: Before, the man was blind. Now he can see.
entries.contrast: See is not hear. You hear with your ears.

qa.q: Do you see with your ears?

def: Wash means to make clean with water.
You wash your hands before you eat. You wash a cup after tea.
Wash is not the same as swim. When you swim, you move in water.
entries.example: The man washes his eyes in the pool.
entries.contrast: Dirty is the opposite of clean.

qa.q: Do you wash with water?

def: Mud is wet earth.
When it rains, the ground is wet, and you can get mud on your shoes.
Mud is soft and brown.
entries.example: Jesus makes mud and puts it on the man's eyes.
entries.contrast: Mud is not water. Mud is not stone. It is earth and water together.

qa.q: Is mud wet earth?

def: A pool is a small place with water.
You can wash in a pool. You can swim in a big pool.
The pool in the story is called Siloam.
entries.example: The man washes in the pool of Siloam.
entries.contrast: A pool is not a river. A river is long and moves.

qa.q: Is a pool a place with water?

def: Sent means someone told you to go somewhere, or someone sent a thing.
A boss sends an email. A mother sends a child to the shop.
Send is the present. Sent is the past.
entries.example: The name Siloam means Sent.
entries.contrast: Sent is not stayed. Stayed means you did not go.

qa.q: Does a mother send a child to the shop?

def: Trouble means a problem with other people. Or a danger.
If you break a window, you have trouble.
The parents do not want trouble.
entries.example: The leaders can punish them.
entries.contrast: Trouble is not fun. Fun means you feel good.

qa.q: Does a person want trouble?

def: Punish means: you do something bad to a person because he did something you do not like.
A teacher can punish a child who does not do the homework.
Punish is not help.
entries.example: The leaders can punish the parents.
entries.contrast: Punish is not reward. A reward is a good thing for good work.

qa.q: Is a punishment a good thing?

def: The law means the rules of God in the Bible time.
The Pharisees teach the law. They want people to keep it.
The law is also the rules of a country: do not steal.
entries.example: The Pharisees are serious about the law.
entries.contrast: The law is not a game.

qa.q: Do the Pharisees teach the law?

def: The Sabbath is a holy day of rest. It is the seventh day.
On the Sabbath, people stop their normal work.
For you, the Sabbath is from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset.
entries.example: It was the Sabbath when Jesus healed the man.
entries.contrast: The Sabbath is not a work day.

qa.q: Is the Sabbath a work day?
qa.a: No, it is a day of rest.

def: Light helps you to see. The sun gives light. A lamp gives light.
When there is no light, it is dark.
Jesus says, "I am the light of the world."
entries.example: The room is dark. Turn on the light.
entries.contrast: Light is the opposite of dark.

qa.q: Does light help you see?

def: Truth is what is real. It is what really happened.
When you tell the truth, you say what is real.
The word has the sound th. Put your tongue between your teeth.
entries.example: He tells the truth.
entries.contrast: Truth is not a lie.

qa.q: Is the truth a lie?

def: Lie means you say something that is not true.
A child says, "I did not break the cup," but he did. That is a lie.
A person who lies is not honest.
entries.example: He doesn't lie.
entries.contrast: Lie is the opposite of tell the truth.

qa.q: Does an honest man lie?

def: A phrase is a short group of words. It is not a whole sentence.
"Afraid of" is a phrase. "He is not afraid of the Pharisees" is a sentence.
We learn phrases inside sentences.
entries.example: Tell the truth is a phrase.
entries.contrast: A phrase is not one word.

qa.q: Is a phrase one word?
qa.a: No. It is a group of words.

def: A definition tells you what a word means.
"Honest means you say the truth" is a definition.
A good definition uses easy words.
entries.example: This book gives a definition for each word.
entries.contrast: A definition is not a story.

qa.q: Does a definition tell you what a word means?

def: A task is a small job in the lesson. An exercise is the same idea.
Your task can be: Repeat. Or: Answer.
You can ask: What is the task?
entries.example: The task is: Repeat the sentence.
entries.contrast: A task is not a test. It is practice.

qa.q: Is a task a small job?

def: In other words means: I say the same idea with easier words.
You use it when someone does not understand.
After it, say the idea in a simple way.
entries.example: He is honest. In other words, he doesn't lie.
entries.contrast: It is not a new idea. It is the same idea.

qa.q: Does it give a new idea?

def: Use it when you do not understand.
It is polite. You ask the teacher to say it once more.
You can add: more slowly, please.
entries.example: Could you say that again, more slowly?
entries.contrast: It is not rude. It is a good question.

qa.q: Is it polite?
